title: Pikon: an AI-assisted Flutter game on iOS and Android, with a Seedance 2.5 trailer
author: Jerome_bonjour
selftext:
I'm the developer of Pikon, a Flutter strategy game that's available on iOS and Android. You align four tokens, the line disappears, and gravity can turn that into a chain reaction.



I've been using AI assistance on the project. For the trailer, I put together references from the game's own assets: the red and blue characters, both boards, token artwork, short gameplay clips and the music. Seedance 2.5 gave me the promotional result I liked best. The earlier videos didn't capture the game's feel well enough.



The 3D world is a separate part of the project, built with flutter\_scene and Flutter GPU. That separation lets me work on the archipelago without running the whole multiplayer flow. Its demo shows a boat, changing weather, conquest effects and a stone wall being built: [https://www.youtube.com/shorts/E56hZT\_j4Ps](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/E56hZT_j4Ps)



The attached video is the animated trailer. The World link above is a development capture using local demo data.



Pikon is free to download, with optional in-app purchases.

App Store: [https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6804834624?pt=129356866&ct=aigamedev&mt=8](https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6804834624?pt=129356866&ct=aigamedev&mt=8)

Google Play: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.jbonjour.pikon&referrer=utm\_source%3Daigamedev%26utm\_medium%3Doutreach](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.jbonjour.pikon&referrer=utm_source%3Daigamedev%26utm_medium%3Doutreach)



I'd be interested in how other people keep generated trailers close to their game's actual look and mechanics.
